properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued August 6 at 7:44AM EDT until August 6 at 8:45AM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
SMWILM

The National Weather Service in Wilmington has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Little River Inlet SC to South Santee River SC from 20
to 60 NM...

* Until 845 AM EDT.

* At 744 AM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near Vermillion Reef, moving north at 10
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Parking Lot Area, Vermillion Reef, Horseshoe Area, and Horseshoe
Reef.
properties.instruction:
Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.
If caught on the open water, prepare for deteriorating conditions.
Make sure you and your crew are wearing properly fitted life jackets.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 6 at 5:24AM CDT until August 8 at 12:20PM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Missouri...

Big Creek at Blairstown affecting Johnson, Cass and Henry Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Big Creek at Blairstown.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, The west bank of the creek begins to flood.
At 23.0 feet, Flooding occurs at the west approach to the N Highway
bridge located 0.2 miles west of Blairstown. Flooding also occurs
across B Highway near Big Creek which is several miles northwest of
Blairstown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:00 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 11.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon to a crest of 21.5 feet this evening. It will then fall
below flood stage early tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 5 at 1:54PM AKDT until August 7 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 146 PM AKDT, river gauge reports indicate rises in water
levels from heavy rain across the warned area. Flooding is
ongoing. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are possible.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 12:50pm the stage was 22.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 22.4 feet is expected around 4:00pm
Wednesday.
-The Yentna River at Lake Creek is forecast to go below flood
stage Saturday morning August 8th.

Impacts:
Between 21 and 22 feet, several lodges may have water in or
around low-lying cabins.




- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 1 PM AKDT FRIDAY

properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Straits of Florida from Ocean Reef to west end of Seven Mile Bridge
20 to 60 nm out...

* Until 800 AM EDT.

* At 724 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located near Elbow Cay,
moving west at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* Locations in the warning include...
Elbow Cay.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 6 at 6:10AM CDT until August 6 at 9:15AM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
FFWLSX

The National Weather Service in St Louis has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Washington County in east central Missouri...

* Until 915 AM CDT.

* At 610 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain
is expected. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly. Areas along Mineral Fork will see rapid rises in the creek
levels.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Potosi, Anthonies Mill, Mineral Point, Old Mines, Richwoods, Latty,
Shirley and Cadet.

This includes the following State Parks...
Washington State Park.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 7.9 feet Monday evening.

properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 6 at 6:18AM CDT until August 6 at 8:15AM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
At 618 AM CDT, the heaviest rain had come to an end. However, flash
flooding was ongoing. Emergency management reported flash flooding
causing road closures. Flash flooding will continue even as the rain
has decreased in intensity.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Washington, Union, Sullivan, Pacific, St. Clair, Villa Ridge, Gray
Summit, Parkway, Miramiguoa Park, Lonedell, Moselle, Piney Park,
Robertsville, Catawissa, Stanton and Lyon.

This includes the following State Parks...
Robertsville State Park and Meramec State Park.

This includes Interstate 44 in Missouri between exits 225 and 257.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.
